title: 20 years in games, first jam ever: Co-Stars (co-op space fighter)
author: anotherbuilddev
selftext:
After making games professionally for 20 years, this was the first game jam I've ever entered: the Epic AI Mega Game Jam. The game is called Co-Stars.

I've been having such a great time building things with modern tools that I wanted to see what I could do (along with nearly 3k other people, it seems).

**Play it (free):** [https://anotherbuild.itch.io/co-stars](https://anotherbuild.itch.io/co-stars)

**Full dev log:** [https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLHDbhPA6zytY](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLHDbhPA6zytY)

# It wasn't just "press a button and get a game"

Some numbers from my Claude Code sessions over the four days:

* **About 1,000 messages** across about 127 sessions, climbing from \~200 on day one to \~330 on the last day
* **About 20,000 words** typed by me, so a typical message was about 20 words
* **About 240 messages were four words or fewer**, like "yes", "do it" or "ship it"
* **About 40 hours of active directing** over a jam that ran about 93 hours on the clock. The rest was agents running overnight while I was away from the keyboard.

Those numbers only cover Claude Code. They leave out the Codex and ElevenLabs sessions.

# Tech stack and tools

**Engine and code**

* Unreal Engine 5.8.4 (C++)
* Unreal MCP plugin
* NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 plugin
* Git + Git LFS

**AI coding and image generation**

* Claude Code (Anthropic)
* Codex (OpenAI), for code and image generation

**3D and materials**

* Hyper3D Rodin: 3D models
* Blender: Python scripts and the PinSolver extension
* PBRgen: PBR materials

**Audio**

* ElevenLabs: voices, music, sound effects, voice changer

**Video**

* Runway Act-Two: cast intro videos from my own webcam performances
* ffmpeg

**Sourced assets**

* Six open-license fonts (SIL OFL / Apache 2.0)
* Unreal Engine basic shapes
* ElevenLabs Voice Library voices

comments.author: anotherbuilddev
comments.body: Have been a fan of games like this since Tie Fighter and decided to get a little silly with this one

comments.author: Electronic-Movie4208
comments.body: That's impressive, man! 😄 Really shows how much work still goes into AIassisted development. I'm building my own RPG called Lanternwake, and it's been quite the journey! Would love to connect and exchange ideas sometime. Congrats on Co-Stars!

replies.author: anotherbuilddev
replies.body: Appreciate the comment! Would be happy to see your project and exchange ideas, shoot me a DM when you are ready :)

replies.author: Electronic-Movie4208
replies.body:
Awesome, thanks! My game's called Lanternwake, a fantasy RPG I'm building with AI assistance. It's still a work in progress, but you can check it out here:

https://solacekingdom.pages.dev/play/solace/

Would love your feedback! Feel free to follow me here on Reddit, and I'll gladly follow you back. Always happy to connect with fellow devs and exchange ideas!

replies.author: anotherbuilddev
replies.body: Nice, I will take a look this week and let you know any comments

replies.author: Electronic-Movie4208
replies.body:
Remember to follow me back! 😀

u/Electronic-Movie4208

comments.author: VortexAssetStudio
comments.body:
People still think AI game dev is just clicking one button, so seeing the actual breakdown of 40 hours of directing and 1,000+ iterations is super refreshing. 

Getting clean, usable 2D sprites and textures out of image models without spending forever fixing broken silhouettes or weird lighting is honestly half the battle. Congrats on shipping it for the jam, grabbing the build on itch to check out that 70s space movie vibe.

replies.author: anotherbuilddev
replies.body: Thank you, I’ve gotten a lot of hate on different sub reddits and platforms for AI projects and people asking me “what is the point.” Which I think might be a bit of a misconception about what it takes. Hope you enjoy and get a friend to play some co-op with you

replies.author: VortexAssetStudio
replies.body: Totally get that, people love to jump on the hate train without seeing the actual pipeline and cleanup work behind the scenes. At the end of the day, players just care if a game is fun to play. Already pinged a buddy to jump into the gunner seat this weekend—keep building!

replies.author: anotherbuilddev
replies.body: Don’t be surprised that it local co-op only for now, maybe someday online. Thanks again for the kind words and all the best to you
